copy_pick.why: Candidate 2 best wears the 1940s newsreel voice, with the grand 'FALL BENEATH THE KREMLIN'S WRATH' headline and the 'Barely had the ink dried' opening, and it avoids yesterday's Trump-Xi-Putin Shenzhen opening and diplomacy-vs-everything closer, which Candidates 1 and 3 both echo.

doom.driver: Three Kyiv bridges hit during major Russian missile attack. Five people were killed in a wave of strikes which follow Ukraine's successful targeting of the Crimean Bridge.
doom.blurb: KYIV'S BRIDGES FALL BENEATH THE KREMLIN'S WRATH
doom.summary: Barely had the ink dried on the Shenzhen 'peace declaration', which somehow didn't mention either war, when Russian missiles took out three Kyiv bridges as payback for Crimea. Meanwhile Iran is escalating in Hormuz, and Anthropic's record IPO arrived just in time to watch global markets have their worst week since 2020. Peace was declared, and nobody told the missiles or the Nasdaq.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: Gemini can now drive your Mac, Apple is building its own agent, and Anthropic went public at a trillion-and-a-half valuation.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: California subpoenas Nvidia while Congress learns 879,000 AI chips were cleared for Chinese buyers.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Russia smashes Kyiv's bridges in retaliation for Crimea, and Iran escalates its attacks on Hormuz shipping.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Chatbots fold on climate facts when users push back, and a school's AI gun detector mistook a Doritos bag for a weapon.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: The AI sell-off is driving the worst week for markets since 2020, and a teenage founder is optimizing missiles for 'cost per kill.'

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. A wide night view of the Dnipro River in Kyiv in the hours after the strikes, seen from the low left-bank embankment. The vast river is a sheet of molten orange and blood-red reflections under a deep violet sky, with drifting smoke and river mist glowing furnace-orange from fires below. Across the water, the high right-bank hills rise with golden-domed Lavra churches lit hellish red from underneath, and the silver Motherland Monument stands tall on the ridge, her sword catching the glare. Dominating the middle distance is a long steel-and-concrete cable-stayed bridge with tall pylons, its deck broken. A jagged gap hangs open in the roadway, twisted guardrails dangle toward the water, and smoke curls up from the wound. Orange cables fan out against the violet sky. In the foreground, wide pools of light from sodium streetlamps and a parked State Emergency Service fire engine with its red and white body and flashing beacons fall on the wet embankment promenade. Police barrier sawhorses with glowing amber lamps block the bridge approach ramp. Two whole rescue workers in orange helmets and reflective vests stand beside the engine, coiling a hose. A neat row of candles and a few bouquets of flowers glow on the low granite parapet beside them. Everything is lit in blood red, furnace orange and bruised violet shadows, with a malevolent glare from below. Every area of the frame is clearly visible and readable at small size.

minor: The two rescue workers are small and blocky, and their hose or coil is a muddy tangle at their feet. Their faces are hidden, so they read as simple figures, not as defects.
The fire engine's cab and body are a little muddled where the front meets the side panel, and the beacons are smeared pink-magenta. It still reads clearly as a fire truck.
The bridge gap is small and the deck ends look jagged. The fire and smoke at the break are readable, but the dangling guardrails are hard to make out.
The police sawhorse barriers on the left ramp are small and blurry, with only a hint of amber lamps.
The candles and flower bouquets on the parapet are clumpy and abstract, but they are recognizable.
The reflections on the river and the wet promenade are streaky and noisy, a side effect of the pixel and color-grade style.
The Motherland Monument and the Lavra domes are simplified and bright. The monument looks gold-pink rather than silver.

dawn.driver: A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks.
dawn.blurb: SEVEN WEEKS SOLO, THE LIVER IS FINE
dawn.summary: In Sydney, a team led by surgeon and inventor Carlo Pulitano kept a human liver alive on life support outside the body for a record seven weeks, a feat that could reshape how organs are studied, repaired and one day transplanted. Out past Venus, the BepiColombo spacecraft is finally settling into orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey. And in a smaller, sweeter story, a man in South Carolina is holding his cat again after three and a half years, thanks to a kind stranger in Oregon.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: A human liver kept working outside the body for seven weeks opens new possibilities for organ preservation and biomedical engineering.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: The UK and EU are expected to agree a youth mobility scheme at their summit, opening doors for young people to live and work across the Channel.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: A woman in Oregon helped reunite a long-lost cat with its owner in South Carolina after three and a half years apart.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Conservationists in South Africa are working to replant five centuries-old baobabs and return them to home soil.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: After eight years of travel, BepiColombo is entering orbit around Mercury to begin exploring the solar system's smallest planet.

copy_pick.why: Candidate 3 keeps the understated voice ('THE LIVER IS FINE') and avoids the recent cards' 'Closer to home' / 'Far from…' transitions and colon-led openers, swapping in a fresh 'Out past Venus' and a warm cat reunion, all good news with no doom framing.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. GROUND-LEVEL VIEW looking steeply upward from the dewy grass verge of a quiet suburban Sydney street on a clean, clear morning. The environment dominates the frame. A colossal Moreton Bay fig towers overhead, its buttress roots and canopy of broad soft-green leaves filling the upper half of the image. Pale amber sunrise light filters through the leaves and spills in warm gold shafts, while the last blue-grey shadows lift from the lawn and the weatherboard front of a Federation-style house. The camera is low among blades of grass and a cracked terracotta garden edge. A short stone path rises toward a raised front porch. On the porch stand a man in his fifties in a loose cardigan, his skin faintly sallow, and his wife in a green sweater. They hold each other, whole figures seen from below. She presses a phone to her ear with her eyes closed and her face crumpling into relief, and he looks up toward the sky with his shoulders finally dropping. A packed navy hospital duffel sits on the top step beside them, and a mug steams on the railing. Seven faded yellow ribbons hang from a low fig branch above the porch, one for each week of waiting, and the newest is still bright. A letterbox in the foreground grass and a sleepy cat on the path add small domestic details. The palette is warm amber, honey gold and soft leaf green, with gentle cream highlights and clarity arriving through the light.

minor: The yellow ribbons hanging from the branch look stiff, like clothespins or tiny hanging figures, and there are six instead of seven. They read as odd shapes but not as a clear defect.
The couple are small and slightly merged together, so the woman's face, phone and raised hand are hard to read. Nothing looks clearly broken at phone size.
The letterbox has an oddly open front and sits right against the tree trunk, which makes it look a little flat.
The mug on the railing from the prompt is not visible.
Foliage and light shafts are busy, and a few leaf edges look jagged, but this fits the pixel-art style.
